name: Chung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only SIL survey-level material known for Chung (Cameroon); no phonology reached

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page cung1238 and reference-table queries (title 'Cung', 'Beboid', 'Chungmboko'; authors Tabah, Langhout, Boutwell)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Brye & Brye 2002 and Ethnologue for Chung; no grammar, sketch or phonology of Chung exists in its bibliography (Beboid hits are Nchane, Mungong, Kemezung, Naami, Sari, Koshin, Mundabli items).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 RA. 2021/2022. Change Request 2021-012 (split [cug] Chungmboko into Chung [cnq] and Mbuk [bpc]) with new-code forms; and Change Request 2016-006 (Cung > Chungmboko, B. Langhout, SIL Misaje)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity and bibliography only: Chung closest to Mbuk and Nchane (83% lexical similarity, Boutwell 2010); literacy program 2011, primer 2012, Luke 2014. No phonology.

sources.citation: Tschonghongei, Nelson C. 2020. Mbuk documentary grammar. PhD dissertation, University of Yaounde I. 615 pp. (KPAAM-CAM)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the sister variety Mbuk [bpc], not Chung. Tone secs. 2.2.4-2.2.5 pp.162-167 (lexical and grammatical tone, H/L/M/F/R patterns by syllable count); sec. 1.4.5.3 p.75 'All the Western Beboid languages are tonal'; sec. 1.4.3.9 'Orthographic accent' pp.68-69 is about Chung-orthography-induced pronunciation, not word accent. No word-stress statement for Mbuk or Chung. Bibliography cites Tabah 2015 'A Preliminary Lexico-Semantic Description of Cung (Chung) Grammar' (SIL Cameroon ms).

sources.citation: Kitu, Christopher, Oliver Shang Kitu, Ernest Trinja Ngong & Genesis Kamenda Ngong. 2012. Nfaa Bə Nyaka Wi Chuŋ / Reading and Writing the Chung Language. Boyo Division: Chung Language Committee. 60 pp. (SIL archives 56472)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Transition primer (letters, exercises, stories); some words carry tone marks but there is no statement on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2002. Rapid appraisal and intelligibility testing surveys of the Eastern Beboid group of languages (Northwest Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-019, 66 pp. (SIL archives 9189)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey only; sec. 3.7 'Cung [886]' p.29 covers intelligibility, language use, origins ('The people of Cung know of nothing written in their language'); no phonology, no tone or stress statement (only 'accent/tone/etc.' in an RTT scoring rubric). Cites Richards 1991 phonologies of Noone, Ncane, Sari, not Cung.

sources.note: Dictionary front matter and the webonary 'Language > Phonology' page normally carry a short phoneme/tone summary for the language; tone-marked headwords would also show the prosodic system.

sources.citation: Tabah, Grace. 2021. Tone description in Eastern Beboid Languages: Implications for Orthography and Literacy. PhD thesis (defended April 2021; covers Naami, Chungmboko and Kemedzung; university not named in the Naami Orthography Guide 2023 that reports it, probably Yaounde I)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only known primary tonal description of Chungmboko (Chung + Mbuk); a thesis-length tone study would state the prosodic type and whether stress plays any role.

sources.citation: Boutwell, Richard L. 2020. A grammar of Nchane: A Bantoid (Beboid) language of Cameroon. PhD dissertation, Leiden University. xxiv+393 pp. (also Boutwell 2014, Nchane phonology sketch, SIL Cameroon)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Closest well-described relative (83% lexical similarity per Boutwell 2010); its prosody chapter would give the expected Eastern Beboid pattern (tone, no stress) as a comparative baseline, but it is not a statement about Chung.

sources.citation: Tabah, Grace. 2011. Cung Orthography Guide. Yaounde: SIL Cameroon. 15 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 98970; file)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: no other copy located; the open copy could not be downloaded when a reader tried
sources.note: The only Chung-specific phonological write-up in existence (alphabet, vowels, consonants and almost certainly a tone section, as in the same author's Naami guide); most likely place for a 'Chung is a tonal language' statement and any remark on stress.

sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Only the catalogue record could be read. The PDF on sil.org/system/files is behind an automated-access block (could not be reached by automated download, direct download and reader proxies), has no archived copy at the Internet Archive, and Save-Page-Now returned 500 six times. Same author's Naami orthography guide (held by the project under bebe1250) has a tone section and no stress statement, so this guide is expected to state tone only.
